name: liquid-glass-weather
title: Liquid Glass Weather
description: A compact weather panel built from translucent glass cards: an hourly strip across the top, the current temperature and a clock beside it, and a five-day forecast below, all over a cloud photo.
use: You need a compact at-a-glance weather panel that layers on top of a photo or gradient.
avoid: White text over white cloud areas drops to near-invisible, so it needs a darker or blurred backdrop.
a11y: White text over bright clouds is hard to read, and the draggable panels offer no keyboard route. (keyboard: partial, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Four white-tinted glass panels of differing widths float over a bright blue sky with white clouds. The top strip lists six hourly slots with small weather icons; below, one panel shows a big temperature, another a clock and a location pill, and a wide panel lists five days with high and low figures.
behaves: Static once drawn: the hourly, current and daily figures never change and no state is wired. Each glass panel can be dragged on its own and springs back, scaling slightly on hover and press.
customise: All temperatures, times, days and the city are typed into the JSX, as is the background photo URL. Panel corners, shadows and glow come from the glass card props.
weight: moderate: Five blurred glass panels with a displacement filter each, over a full photo.
